recommendations.text: Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in patients undergoing a primary PCI strategy.
Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in NSTE-ACS patients who are not expected to undergo an early invasive strategy (<24 h) and do not have HBR.
Pre-treatment with a GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist is not recommended.
Routine pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in NSTE-ACS patients in whom coronary anatomy is not known and early invasive management (<24 h) is planned is not recommended.
Parenteral anticoagulation is recommended for all patients with ACS at the time of diagnosis.
Routine use of a UFH bolus (weight-adjusted i.v. bolus during PCI of 70–100 IU/kg) is recommended in patients undergoing PCI.
Intravenous enoxaparin at the time of PCI should be considered in patients pre-treated with subcutaneous enoxaparin.
Discontinuation of parenteral anticoagulation should be considered immediately after an invasive procedure.
Enoxaparin should be considered as an alternative to UFH in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI.
Bivalirudin with a full-dose post PCI infusion should be considered as an alternative to UFH in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI.
Fondaparinux is not recommended in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI.
For patients with NSTE-ACS in whom early invasive angiography (i.e. within 24 h) is not anticipated, fondaparinux is recommended.

genes.context: The guideline repeatedly refers to 'P2Y12 receptor inhibitor' pre-treatment recommendations in patients undergoing primary PCI and in NSTE-ACS, and states routine pre-treatment in certain NSTE-ACS scenarios is not recommended.
